why: T1 constrains the LP optimum at n=m², not at primes. A valid n-dependent constraint can have RHS 0 at squares and positive RHS at primes; M_BM is an explicit example of square-sensitive data. The implication that such a constraint must encode the answer is unproved. The 56-by-54 finite dictionary test excludes only that dictionary; FRONTIER §6 explicitly leaves growing-level identities open.
should_be: unclear; growing-level character-sensitive LP minorant, plausibility 1; keep

why: For a FIXED finite list a b^s+c with b>1, there are O(log X) values up to X, hence zero relative prime density. This proves that list cannot cover a positive proportion. A growing list has no such cardinality bound. B1/B2 collapse is not a theorem forbidding all growing lists, and the master asks about primes within a family, not coverage of every prime.
should_be: known-false for fixed exponential-menu coverage; unclear for growing menus; prime production is a separate side problem

why: Let r=4/p-1/x-1/y=a/b>0 in lowest terms. Completion by 1/z is equivalent to a=1 (then z=b). Bounds making r small do not force a=1. Alternatively, for e=4x-p, (ey-px)(ez-px)=(px)^2 is exactly the two-term divisor condition. Thus the supplied exact-completion target has no independent near-miss input.
should_be: circular exact-completion target; near-miss estimates alone have no ES yield

why: The finite-menu assertion for every p is unconditionally false at p=409: checks.json exhausts all 1≤C≤102 and finds no divisor in -1 mod 4C, hence none for C=1,2,3,6. The bound follows from p=4CuB-u-B≥4C-2. Unit groups of exponent 2 occur here exactly when 4C divides 24; outside these levels a single quadratic sign cannot specify -1. Infinitely many failures still needs the stated H hypothesis.
should_be: known-false for the stated all-prime fixed menu (CERTIFIED 409); growing levels open

why: CONDITIONAL_ES Prop 2.3 gives M≤2μ f. Together with ET average counts this excludes M≥p^η for all large primes when μ=p^{o(1)}. That proves the claimed power-size bounded-fibre version false, but the row never requires d≥p^κ or bounded fibres in its missing theorem; d≤p^{O(1)} alone is insufficient. Subconvexity itself is not false or excluded in every encoding.
should_be: known-false after adding power-size target and bounded-fibre hypotheses; unclear otherwise

why: A dispersion/second-moment lower bound at fixed p is not contradicted by a small-range numerical exponent budget. B3 forbids power-size target counts with bounded fibres, not a one-sided polylog lower bound. Correlations over p diagnose an average leak, not a counterexample at every large p. No theorem or counterexample refutes the missing estimate.
should_be: open hard; plausibility 1; first seek a class-aware dyadic saving (FRONTIER §7.1)

why: The displayed |X|≤(1-ε)M_gen is TWO-sided, despite the prose calling it one-sided. BM_CORRECTED_COUNT Prop 3.1 supplies an infinite upper-tail obstruction to polylog two-sided errors, not an equivalence proof. For a correctly defined genus residual R-M_gen, the useful repair is X≥-(1-ε)M_gen. Moving conductor and sparse divisors defeat a direct FKM application, not all geometric cancellation.
should_be: known-false for the global polylog absolute-error target; open hard for one-sided or weaker cancellation; retain repaired lane

why: The displayed lower bound is a quantitative strengthening of eventual (★) existence, not logically equivalent to ES: (★) is already a subfamily, and ES does not imply a uniform count floor. MRT averages interval locations and concerns fixed multiplicative functions, whereas C↦D^-_{4C}(4Cp+1) has moving modulus. This is a real applicability gap, not a no-go theorem for all C-uniformity arguments.
should_be: open hard quantitative tied-divisor lower tail; plausibility 1, no Gowers input supplied

why: From p=4CuB-u-B≥4C-2, winning C form a finite set for fixed p. A nonempty return-time set to an open set of a minimal compact dynamical system is syndetic, hence infinite. Therefore the exact proposed return-time identification is impossible. In addition checks.json verifies no winners at p=409. Finite-orbit or truncated-time models would be different claims.
should_be: known-false for the minimal-system return-time model

why: A certificate-producing short vector is equivalent to a certificate only AFTER the cone and residue dictionary is specified. Equidistribution of a separate auxiliary lattice family is a stronger potential input, not an equivalent assertion. AES hypotheses about spheres and lattice shapes are not established here; B3 excludes low-multiplicity power-size targets but allows sparse targets or large fibres (Remark 2.4).
should_be: unclear auxiliary-lattice shrinking-target theorem; no known usable AES transfer

why: For p≡1 mod4, the lens homotopy classification has qq′=±square, with -1 square, so nontrivial homotopy class means (A/p)=-1. Negative-definite linear plumbings with coefficients ≥2 encode the HJ expansion; a chain of length ≤3 is exactly the stated ES5 target. This is an equivalent restricted certificate problem, not an equivalence ES⇔ES5 (FRONTIER §7.14 remains open).
should_be: circular as an ES5 dictionary; no filling-existence theorem supplied

why: Avoiding 3 is strictly additional to ES and is not equivalent to the unrestricted tied-divisor event. All eight solutions at 241 do meet 3 (independently enumerated in checks.json), but the theorem explicitly excludes 241. Moreover this is not a 3-adic obstruction: (n,n,n/2) is a positive rational, 3-adic-unit solution for n=241. The global exceptional classification is a legitimate new side target, with no known proof handle.
should_be: open hard restricted ES; plausibility 1 for universality, 3 for finite exact/local classification; retain

why: BL Thm 1.8 supplies the positive-real integral-adelic BM premise for every n≥2. Thus on this family the implication BM-soluble⇒positive integral point asserts exactly the desired conclusion. At primes it is ES(p), with scaling giving all n. Markoff non-BM failures are caution, not counterexamples to ES.
should_be: circular for the proposed ES-family Hasse principle

why: Every nonsquare prime has a QNR, so an unrestricted QNR⇒some certificate implication merely supplies the (★) conclusion once its premise is known. But a level bound t≤4ℓ is a stronger, falsifiable assertion, not an equivalence. The theorem in SS9 proves a positive BM coset count, not the class -1; 409 refutes any all-prime (★) conclusion. Allowing a threshold and genuine class-control is still open (§7.3).
should_be: open hard beyond-BM class control with a threshold; no direct implication from least QNR known

why: Read ident_form_families §§3–6: Prop 3.2 handles Type II polynomial coordinates for positive-definite quadratics; Lemma 3.3 only constrains Type I e; the Gaussian trap for t²+1 uses Hypothesis H. It is not an unconditional no-go for every listed P, especially quartics. The same source explicitly leaves nonconstant-level Type I families open and exhibits t²+21 identities in Mordell-hard classes.
should_be: conditional obstruction for bounded t²+1 procedures; scoped Type II theorem; unclear for nonconstant Type I/general P

why: The union assertion R_star(p)+R_b1(p)>0 is an ES-strength subfamily target. A particular explicit injection/switch with a tractable deficit bound is extra structure: the union assertion does not imply such a map. Calling every possible switch circular just because its output is a divisor certificate conflates a sufficient mechanism with its conclusion. No counterexample or nonexistence theorem for switching is cited.
should_be: unclear, plausibility 1; complementary-line switching is a legitimate unconstructed mechanism

why: A bounded NUMBER of candidates 2^k m is not a fixed menu of polynomial slices: k≈log2 p changes with p, outside B1 finite formal-run assumptions. Also x∈(p/4,3p/4] only bounds the smallest denominator, not the distinguished one without further argument. checks.json gives actual failures for M=1 (including 73), but proves nothing for every fixed M or positive density. The universal all-M verdict is unsupported.
should_be: known-false at M=1 by finite check; general fixed-M failure theorem unclear; retain as calibration

why: The master names no precise denominator set D_p. With all positive denominators, a three-term representation is ES by definition; with a genuinely restricted D_p it is stronger, not equivalent without showing every ES witness belongs to D_p. Unbounded-term Erdős–Graham theorems do not give a three-term statement. Correct gap, incomplete claimed equivalence.
should_be: circular for unrestricted three-term target; unspecified/unclear for a restricted set

why: For D consisting of divisors of N, Σ_{d∈D}1/d≤σ(N)/N≪log log N. This does miss Bloom Thm 3 at X comparable to N. The cited memo §3.1 also derives a many-term lower bound for Bloom Prop 1. This disproves direct applicability of those hypotheses, not every reciprocal-mass lemma on structured divisors, nor an ES-specific three-term lemma.
should_be: inapplicable named theorem; unclear structured mass lemma, not known-false in general

why: For positive integers u,v, 1/u+1/v≤2. Thus it cannot equal an integer ℓ≡3 mod4 (ℓ≥3). This is the precise unit-sum mechanism of other_rings Lemma 3.1, so the literal transfer is false. Pell-type replacements with p-dependent divisibility would be different mechanisms.
should_be: known-false for the literal integer unit-sum transfer

why: A finite ET covering of every least-QNR-r class is contradicted by the sterile r-generic point theorem for large r (FRONTIER §5.3). But F_q as the implication (q/p)=-1⇒ES(p) is not equivalent to a finite identity covering. ES being true on residue classes need not have a polynomial proof there. Thus the covering version is blocked; unrestricted F_q is not refuted.
should_be: known-false for the finite-covering proposal; open for unrestricted F_q

why: QUATERNION_ES Prop 2.2 shows the SPECIFIED quaternion dictionary leaves X²-Y²=4m with e|X. It does not quantify over every possible order or norm-like map. gon_fermat_certificates §5 explicitly notes exact geometry-of-numbers existence escapes the power-size B3 argument. No universal no-go for an unspecified order R follows. Fixed congruence-only norm criteria are inadequate, but the broad target is unconstructed, not known-false.
should_be: unclear, plausibility 1 only after specifying R and a conversion; retain without treating it as a concrete lead

why: The asserted equivalence is wrong. At p=409,C=1, X=819,Y=818 give X²-Y²=1637 and X≡-1 mod2C, yet factors 1,1637 are both +1 mod4 and there is no (★) hit at any C. The weak condition holds for every p at C=1 with X=2p+1,Y=2p. Correct condition is X-Y≡X+Y≡-1 mod4C; THEN factorisation is exactly the divisor event.
should_be: known-true but useless weak Fermat identity; corrected two-factor congruence is circular; no revived proof mechanism

why: A dense set containing a polynomial configuration does not imply membership of each prescribed p. Finite polynomial coverings have the B1 obstruction; the source does not prove every growing polynomial-configuration architecture false. The phrase that polynomial families cannot cover square classes also needs its modulus/linear-parameter scope (see Z1296).
should_be: named density theorem inapplicable to every p; fixed-cover variant blocked; growing variant unclear

why: B3 does not refute effective equidistribution at measure μ(Ω_p) if the target main term is polylog. CONDITIONAL_ES Remark 2.4 expressly allows power-small error relative to such a main term. Duke currently resolving larger targets is a limitation of known estimates, not a counterexample to the requested shrinking-target theorem. No fibre bound or precise region was supplied either.
should_be: open hard/unclear shrinking-target theorem; plausibility 1, no known estimate at required scale

why: For nonempty A,B⊂F_p*, |AB|≥max(|A|,|B|), not generally |A||B| (take A=B a subgroup). Thus a genuinely p^{o(1)} S3 cannot contain A,B of size p^ε, so the all-large-p product-box plan is incompatible with the subpower-count regime. But |S3(p)|≈log²p is an average/model scale, not a proved pointwise bound; very large upper tails exist. Also arbitrary ε does not suffice for a bilinear character bound.
should_be: power-size product-set route blocked at typical primes; fix the product-size and pointwise claims

why: For fixed (c,d), f|p²+4c²d with f≡-p mod4cd concerns arithmetic factors, not a drop in the Galois group of one fixed finite cover. Fixing f reduces it to congruences. This demonstrates the proposed cover is missing, not that every possible auxiliary cover is impossible; CLASS_FORCING only controls specified fixed data.
should_be: unclear until an actual cover and integral-point map are defined; present HIT application unsupported

why: For residue measures δ_p on the profinite units choose increasing primes p_k≡1 mod k!: Dirichlet supplies them and δ_{p_k}→δ_1, not Haar. So universal Haar rigidity of residue data is false. Normalising by certificate count is undefined at a zero. A different measure of ambient candidates could still be defined and have non-congruential information; the broad claim is not refuted by B1 alone.
should_be: known-false for universal residue-Haar model; unclear for a new ambient candidate measure

why: PROPAGATION_CLOSURE §3 explicitly leaves rule Λ open and warns divisor-output form is not a universal no-go. Indeed sharing two denominators can reach a prime without scaling: 4/4=1/2+1/4+1/4 and 4/5=1/2+1/4+1/20 (checked). A universal descent would need an independent coverage/rank theorem, which is unknown rather than refuted.
should_be: unclear, plausibility 1; non-scaling transport exists locally, no global descent known

why: Measuring a residual variance is not circular; it is a falsifiable statistical task. H^-_BM is a quantitative strengthening of eventual (★) existence, not equivalent to ES, and a regression does not establish it. The row is right that fitting a main term supplies no pointwise residual lower bound; it is wrong to use that as the status of the measurement.
should_be: EVIDENCE/calibration; open hard for a pointwise lower-tail upgrade

why: Finite polynomial coverings of all prime targets meet Mordell–Schinzel/B1, but the assertion that no curve covers any square class mod840 is false: n=5881+9240k is 1 mod840 and has x=(3n+1)/11,y=3n,z=3nx, verified in checks.json. Higher-degree parameter families can also hit Mordell-hard primes (ident_form_families Prop 3.4). Per-fibre curve classification remains a legitimate finite symbolic task.
should_be: finite universal-cover route blocked; low-degree classification open/tractable, not excluded from hard mod840 classes

why: With the specified HJ/Farey dictionary, the demanded bounded path is precisely an A with (A/p)=-1 and HJ length≤3, i.e. ES5. No independent diameter or path-production theorem is supplied. Expansion giving logarithmic length proves a weaker relaxation, not the required length-three event.
should_be: circular ES5 target, not a proof that graph methods are impossible

why: Three positive steps subtracting 1/x,1/y,1/z reach 0 from 4/p iff their sum equals 4/p, exactly ES. Such steps are not automatically edges of the ordinary Farey graph (determinant-one adjacency), so that language supplies no extra theorem. The HJ version is a restricted ES5 dictionary, not an asserted ES⇔ES5 equivalence.
should_be: circular for the stated unit-fraction path

why: The minimal resolution of 1/p(1,A) is determined by the negative HJ expansion p/A. Requiring three curves and (A/p)=-1 is exactly the length-three restricted certificate event; ≤3 gives the full short-HJ version. Riemenschneider data derived from the same (p,A) do not independently produce A. No new existence input is identified.
should_be: circular short-HJ dictionary (keep exactly-three versus ≤3 convention explicit)

why: The missing theorem only asks for identities covering MORE classes, not all primes. Such identities are possible, including classes hard mod840: x=(3n+1)/11,y=3n,z=3nx for n=5881 mod9240 (all 1 mod840). Mordell–Schinzel forbids a universal finite polynomial cover, not new partial covers or SMT discovery. This is a real partial-result/tool task, albeit not a full ES plan.
should_be: known-true possibility of additional covers; plausibility 3 for automated bounded search; partial yield only

why: Parallel conductance is 1/R=1/x+1/y+1/z. Substituting R=n/4 gives exactly 4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z. The target quantifies over the very same positive integer triples, so it is genuinely equivalent, with no extra network reduction supplied.
should_be: circular three-resistor reformulation

why: For a finite search and nonnegative integer distance, lim_{β→∞}Z_p(β) counts zero-distance certificates; claiming a positive limit is therefore ES. But zero-freeness for every finite β does NOT imply this: exp(-β) is entire, nonzero everywhere, and tends to zero. Thus the proposed analytic implication has a concrete counterexample, beyond the circular endpoint.
should_be: invalid zero-free⇒positive-limit inference; positive zero-temperature limit is circular

why: The row explicitly allows an averaged lower-tail theorem. A coupling/comparison with a product measure plus a relative-entropy bound is neither equivalent to ES nor automatically false because fixed-p indicators are deterministic. It could yield a non-CRT exceptional-set improvement. The missing independent-variable approximation is substantial and unproved; standard KS hypotheses have not been checked. B6 limits yield, it does not refute the partial theorem.
should_be: open hard non-CRT averaged lower tail (§7.5/§7.12); plausibility 1; retain

why: The master asks for a finite minimum and comparison of normalisations, an empirical task. ESC(p)≥c log²p is a quantitative strengthening, not equivalent to ES or mere certificate existence; coordinates may count multiple words per solution. Correct that a nicer normalisation is not a lower-bound proof. Incorrect to mark the empirical question itself circular.
should_be: EVIDENCE/calibration; open hard for uniform positive count floor

why: Privacy follows exactly from gcd(4Cp+1,4C′p+1)|C-C′, since 4 is invertible modulo those odd common divisors. A prime >K touches at most one level C≤K. This excludes pooling those primes into cross-level collisions, not an incidence argument using each private prime in its own level, mixed small/large factors, or growing configurations. No counterexample to the all-large-p claim is supplied.
should_be: unclear incidence lower-bound mechanism; plausibility 1 only after specifying incidence sets and target
